approved: Classification (Publications, Films and Computer Games) Amendment (Industry Self-Classification and Other Measures) Bill 2023
Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications and the Arts
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill updates the national classification system to handle the rising volume of content, especially online, and to cut costs and boost compliance.

The bill lets content providers use government-trained and accredited classifiers to self-classify films and computer games, and gives the Classification Board stronger powers to check and revoke those decisions.
It also creates new exemptions for low-risk cultural material, such as non-English films in public libraries rated G or PG, and broadens rules for cultural institutions.
Expands industry self-classification for films and computer games using accredited classifiers.
Strengthens the Classification Board's ability to quality-assure and revoke self-classification decisions.
Extends classification exemptions to increase access to low-risk cultural content in libraries and approved institutions.
Deems certain content already classified under broadcasting laws as classified under the Classification Act.
Content providers, the Classification Board, public libraries, and approved cultural institutions are affected.
Classification (Publications, Films and Computer Games) Amendment (Industry Self-Classification and Other Measures) Act 2023
